1.point: Open with the contrast between a journey in miles and the journey to God, show that the distance lies on our side, and announce that the chapter sets out the stages of that journey, why it covers no distance and why the stages come in order.
steps: Hook: the pilgrim's journey is measured in miles; the Munajat names another journey, to a God who is Near even to the one who is away.
If God is near to the one who is away, the cause of being away must lie on our side; Abu Hamza names it.
The cause is our deeds, standing as a veil; so the journey is a removal, not a crossing, and the chapter will set out its stages and their order.

2.point: Because God is already nearer than the jugular vein, the journey to Him crosses no distance; it is an inward removal of veils, the dark ones our deeds make and the veils of light that are not ours.
steps: God is already near: Surah Qaf, nearer than the jugular vein.
That nearness is set beside His knowledge of the soul's whispers, so it points inward; there is no distance to cross.
So the journey runs inward: wayfaring is finding ourselves, not moving from place to place.
What the inward journey does is lift the veil over the heart that blocks its vision of God.
The veils are of two kinds: dark veils, made by our deeds and removable by our deeds; veils of light, from our creaturehood, lifted (where they lift) at the end.
Either way the obstacle is on our side, so the journey is the removal of veils inside us.

3.point: The veils are removed in four stages, polishing, emptying, adorning and passing away, of which the first two are the traveller's work and the last two are God's act.
steps: The mystics count four stages to the end of the first journey; name them.
Polishing: wake, repent, keep the law strictly; removes the dark veils; our work.
Emptying: clear the heart of all but God through the five disciplines; our work.
Adorning: gifts the soul cannot make for itself, including love of God; God's act.
Passing away: God shows His glory and the self, the last veil, falls; God's act.
Hence the stages fall into two pairs: two ours, two God's.

4.point: The four stages come in a fixed order because each depends on the one before, and no stage is left behind when the next begins.
steps: Each stage needs the one before: no moving on until polished; only a purified soul catches God's gifts; passing away comes when adorning reaches its height.
No stage is dropped: polishing accompanies the mystic to the end, the Prophet still kept vigil, the law is kept more carefully after unveiling; each stage is added to those before it.

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Supplies the hook (journey in miles vs the other journey) and the first step: God is the Near One, so the distance is not on His side.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Draws the inference the opening needs: if God is near, what makes a person away is on our side; introduces the prayer that names it.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Supplies the answer (deeds as veil), converts the journey from a crossing to a removal, and states what the chapter will establish. The opening's job is done here.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the first step of the section: God is already near, grounded in Surah Qaf. (Its first sentence already asserts the section's conclusion; the conclusion then returns in ¶12.)

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Reads the verse: nearer than the jugular vein, and the pairing with the soul's whispers turns the nearness inward. ¶6 opens from exactly this ('with no distance to cross, the journey runs inward').

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Supplies the step 'the journey runs inward, it is finding ourselves'. The suluk/salik terms and the conduct etymology are extras inside a paragraph the chain needs.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Supplies what the inward journey does: lift the veil over the heart. Without it 'removes veils' in the point has no ground.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Introduces the division into dark veils and veils of light, which ¶9-¶10, ¶12 and Section 3 (polishing removes the dark veils) all use. It is a thin signpost that could be folded into ¶9's first sentence, but the division first appears here.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Defines the dark veils: made by our deeds, so removable by our deeds, so the road begins there. ¶14 and the box rely on this. The Abu Hamza gloss repeats ¶3 but the definition is new.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Defines the veils of light: not ours, lifted only at the end, which ¶12 and ¶17 use. The sentence that some never lift even for the Prophet is a side remark the section does not use.

¶11.label: restate
¶11.why: 'The veils lie on our side' and 'no hindrance from the other side' were already made in ¶1 (distance not on God's side), ¶3 (God conceals Himself from no one) and ¶9. ¶10 already placed the light veils on our side too. The quotation is new evidence for a step already taken.

¶12.label: restate
¶12.why: Summary of the section; the point was stated in ¶4's first sentence and argued through ¶5-¶10. Nothing new.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Supplies the count and names of the four stages and the frame (first journey, one chapter each) that ¶14-¶18 fill.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Stage one: what polishing is, when it starts, that it removes the dark veils and is our work.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Stage two: the work moves to the heart; the five disciplines are its tools; still ours. The wine/evil-thoughts contrast is an illustration the step uses to show why the heart is harder.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Stage three: gifts no effort can make, including love; God's act. First appearance of the ours/God's divide that ¶18 states.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Stage four: the self, the last veil, falls before God's glory. The Amuli quotation and the mention of baqa' are extras, but the stage itself is a step the point needs.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Supplies the grouping the point turns on: two stages ours, two God's, with the lecture's words as warrant. Not stated as a pair before this.

¶19.label: restate
¶19.why: Restates the section's point, which ¶13 opened with and ¶18 has just concluded; the box has also just set it out.

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Supplies the first step: fixed order because each stage needs the one before, with warrant for each junction (polish before moving on; only a purified soul catches gifts; fana' when adorning is at its height).

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Supplies the second step: none dropped, with the lecture's words, the Prophet's vigil and the Chapter Six result. With ¶20 the point is complete.

¶22.label: aside
¶22.why: That the road begins where a law-keeping believer stands, and that one need not wait for a teacher, is a corollary the point (order, none dropped) does not need; 'irfan proper begins at stage two' is already in the box. Deleting it leaves ¶20-¶21 and ¶25 intact. Its only user is ¶26, the forward hook, which is not part of this section's argument.

¶23.label: aside
¶23.why: The four journeys of the mystics are a wider map; the section's point concerns the order of the four stages. ¶13 already said the stages end the 'first journey', so ¶24's 'this first journey' still reads without ¶23. A new topic raised and not used.

¶24.label: aside
¶24.why: A second scholar (Ibn Sina, with Tusi in the box) saying the order is the same. ¶20 already carries its warrant from the lectures; nothing later depends on Ibn Sina's count. Corroboration, not a link.

¶25.label: restate
¶25.why: Chapter summary: no distance (¶12), four stages in two pairs (¶19), order and none dropped (¶20-¶21). Every clause has been stated and most of them twice.

¶26.label: restate
¶26.why: Its claim, that the first stage begins with a step any believer can take, is ¶22 again, now as a forward hook ending in a question the chapter does not answer.
